Philippines

The Philippines is an archipelagic nation of over 7,600 islands in Southeast Asia, known for its diverse culture, vibrant economy, and rich history.

Overview

The Republic of the Philippines consists of about 7,641 islands covering roughly 300,000 km². With a population exceeding 114 million, it ranks as the world's 13th most‑populous country. Manila is the capital, while Quezon City is the most populated city.

  • Population: 114 million (2024)
  • Area: ~300,000 km²
  • Capital: Manila

Geography

The archipelago is divided into three major regions—Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao—bordered by the South China Sea, Philippine Sea and Celebes Sea. Its terrain ranges from volcanic mountains to tropical beaches.

01

Islands: ~7,600

02

Highest point: Mount Apo (2,954 m)

03

Major seas: South China, Philippine, Celebes

Timeline

History

Early Austronesian settlers were followed by Spanish colonization in 1521, American rule after 1898, and independence in 1946. The nation’s history blends indigenous, Asian, European and American influences.

  1. 1521Magellan arrives, first European contact
  2. 1898Spain cedes Philippines to the United States
  3. 1946Full independence declared
  4. 1986People Power Revolution restores democracy

Economy

The Philippine economy is a mix of agriculture, services and manufacturing. Electronics and high‑tech exports lead trade, while remittances from overseas Filipino workers contribute heavily to GDP.

  • GDP (2024): $502 billion (nominal)
  • Key exports: electronics, semiconductors, garments
  • Remittances: over $30 billion annually

Culture & Tourism

Filipinos are known for hospitality, vibrant festivals, and a blend of Catholic and indigenous traditions. Tourist hotspots include Boracay, Palawan, and historic Intramuros.

01

Official languages: Filipino, English

02

Major festivals: Sinulog, Ati‑Atihan

03

Top destinations: Palawan, Boracay, Cebu

The Philippines is a nation of islands, cultures, and endless smiles.
